thread:
maya: Heads up — canary token/sec is down ~25% after the v2.3.7 deploy. Seeing many tiny batches and queueing spikes. Dropping the rollout for now, cc @ryan @anika

deploy-bot: Deployment started: release v2.3.7 (canary) — build 2026-03-18T10:25:35Z

ryan: Thanks. Any graphs or profiler dumps? Is this queueing or kernel fallout?

maya: Quick grab from the profiler + scheduler metrics:
```
sched.avg_batch_size_per_shard = 2.1  # expected ~6.5 for this traffic
sched.queue_delay_p50 = 42ms -> p95 320ms
kv_cache.hitrate = 0.52  (baseline ~0.78)
kernel.select_path: small-batch-memcopy used 87% of calls
tokens/sec(canary) down 24% relative to pre-deploy
```

anika: Oof. That smells like the new prefetch/pacing tweak. I think PR #7421 changed the coalesce window and prefetch age heuristics last night. Can we bisect? Might be rollout-blocker.

ci-bot: CI Perf Alert: integration/inference_perf (batcher_packing_test) latency +15% on canary. URL: https://ci.internal/reports/7421/perf

sam: Running a quick local bisect now. I can confirm an obvious behavioral change in the scheduler starting at commit d2f1a9. Will paste the diff that matters.

sam: Bisect snippet:
```diff
- prefetch_age_ms = 20
- coalesce_weight = 1.0
+ prefetch_age_ms = 5
+ coalesce_weight = 0.4
```
That reduces the window where we coalesce incoming reqs, so avg batch sizes collapsed.

maya: Also seeing kernel routing changes in profiler: when batch_size < 4 we take the memcpy fallback kernel which is dramatically slower per-token. Before the change batches > 6 hit the optimized aten kernel.

ryan: OK, hold rollout. I'm opening a rollback PR and a hold on the canary.

ryan: PR created: #7489 revert d2f1a9 (revert prefetch/pacing tweak) — https://git.internal/pulls/7489

deploy-bot: Canary halted for release v2.3.7. Rollback initiated by ryan.

sam: Bisect logs attached: commit message "adaptive_prefetch: lower threshold for re-queuing". The patch aggressively shortened prefetch age and deprioritized coalescing weight; that aligns with the drop in kv hitrate and smaller batches.

anika: We should add a guard: don't route to memcpy/small-batch kernel unless batch_size_per_gpu >= 3 and kv_hitrate < 0.3. Also add a regression test for 'kernel-fallback' under small-batch traffic.

sre-bot: Alert: error budget consumption +3% in the last 10m for canary cluster; token/sec and p95 latency correlate with the deploy window.

maya: Rollback is showing early recovery on canary: avg_batch_size trending back to ~6.7 and tokens/sec normalizing. I'll keep an eye on traces and KV hit rate for a few more cycles.

ryan: Thanks everyone. Leave rollout on hold until we ship a guarded patch + perf test. Follow-up: schedule a short postmortem and add canary perf gating to the deploy job.

maya: Agreed. I'll create a short incident note and link the bisect artifacts.

sam: Will open a patch that reintroduces the adaptive prefetch but with conservative thresholds + unit/perf tests.

maya: 👍
